lines: I remember you! Mostly. You were the not-scary part of the scary bit.
You helped me be me again. I am very attached to being me.
You helped pull me back when even my name felt far away.
I remember cold, hunger, and then your face cutting through the fog.
Being cured is not like waking from sleep. It is more like being returned piece by piece.
Some part of me still listens for that old <shake>groan</shake>. I hate that part.
You helped me back. I may not say it gracefully, but I know what that means.
The village feels different now. Brighter, maybe. Or maybe I can finally notice it again.
I owe you more than a discount and less than my whole life. I am still deciding where that lands.
Do not make a ceremony of it. Just know I remember.
I can taste bread again without thinking it is disappointing. That feels important.
The village sounds like home now instead of dinner. You fixed more than my skin.
I woke with a headache, clean hands, and a future. Good work.
You cured me, and now I get to make ordinary mistakes again.
I do not have grand words. I have a very sincere hello and all my fingers.
Every silly thought in my head belongs to me again. I missed them.
I owe you thanks for every neighbor I can look at without hunger.
The cold left slowly, but it left. You were there the whole time.
I remember enough to know you risked yourself for me.
If I seem glad to see you, it is because I am. No mystery there.
I know your face. Did we meet before or after I stopped groaning?
There was an apple, but not the normal apple kind of day.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember being cold. Then I remember being too warm. Were you there for both?
You smell familiar, which is a strange thing to say out loud.
Did you put me behind bars, or did you let me out? I think both were helpful.
I dreamed that my arms were green. Everyone says that part happened.
There is a blank place in my memory shaped a little like you.
I remember your boots by the door and an apple I did not want to eat.
Was I trying to bite you? Please say I missed.
My head says we are friends. My knees say something frightening happened.
I woke up with a blanket and no idea why everyone looked relieved.
The cure feels like yesterday and a story somebody told me years ago.
I remember a weakness potion. Or rain. Something splashed.
You kept saying my name. I think that helped me find it.
Were those iron bars always there, or was that part of the fever?
I know I should thank you. I am still finding the memory that explains how much.
I remember the sound of my own groan. I wish that bit had gone missing.
Everything before waking is tangled, but you are in the knot somewhere.
If we have already had this conversation, thank you again. It still counts.
I remember some of it, and I would like to remember less of it.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
I am grateful, but please do not come any closer yet.
Your face was there when I woke. My fear has not learned what that means.
I know the chains kept everyone safe. I still hear them when you move.
You saved me. That does not make the memory gentle.
Give me time to put your help and my fear in different places.
I remember reaching for you with teeth. I cannot laugh about that yet.
The apple tasted wrong, and then everything hurt. Please let me have some room.
I believe you meant to help. My body still expects the cage.
Thank you for the cure. Now let me decide when we speak about it.
I woke human and terrified. Both feelings are still here.
Do not touch me without warning. Even kindness makes me flinch lately.
Part of me knows you are safe. The rest is slower to understand.
I am not angry with you. I am angry that any of it happened.
You did the right thing. It still felt like a nightmare from my side.
I can thank you from here. Here is a good distance.
The groaning stopped. The bad dreams have not caught up yet.
I remember enough to trust you a little and fear the memory a lot.
